name: Exchange: knights, Bg4, e6, castle
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nf3 Nf6 Be2 Nc6 O-O Bg4 c3 e6 Bf4 Be7 Nbd2 O-O Re1
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the quiet Exchange, Black develops both knights first, puts the light bishop on g4 before playing ...e6, then finishes with ...Be7 and castling. The symmetrical structure gives White nothing special.

name: Panov: solid ...e6, then ...dxc4 and ...b6/...Bb7
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Be7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 O-O O-O b6
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When White hits d5 with c4, Black shores up the centre with ...e6 at once. Taking on c4 only after the bishop has moved costs White a second bishop move; Black then castles and fianchettoes the light bishop on b7.

name: Blackmar-Diemer style f3: give the pawn back with ...e3
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 f3 e3 Bxe3
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: If White offers the e4 pawn with f3 to build a big lead in development, Black simply pushes ...e3 and returns the pawn, leaving White an awkward e3 bishop and a loosened kingside.

name: Classical 4...Nf6 5.Nxf6+ exf6 (Tartakower)
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ exf6 c3 Bd6 Bd3 O-O
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Recapturing toward the centre with the e-pawn gives doubled f-pawns, but they form a shield around the castled king. The plan is short: bishop to d6 and castle.

name: Classical 4...Nf6 5.Nxf6+ gxf6 (Bronstein-Larsen)
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ gxf6
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The sharper recapture opens the g-file for Black's rooks; the idea is quick queenside development and castling long, then using the half-open file against White's king.

name: Classical 4...Nf6 5.Ng3 h5 harassing the knight
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Ng3 h5
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When the knight retreats to g3 instead of trading, the h-pawn runs at it: ...h5 and ...h4 kick it again, and players who retreat passively lose time.

name: Classical 4...Bf5: keep the bishop room on h7
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The main line develops the light bishop with tempo on the e4 knight. When White chases it with h4-h5, Black answers ...h6 so the bishop always has h7 to retreat to.

name: Fantasy 3.f3: fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Be3
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the Fantasy, Black does not take on e4 and give White a big centre; instead the bishop goes to g7 and Black chips at d4 and e4 over time.

name: Fantasy 3.f3 dxe4 4.fxe4 e5: the dxe5 Qh4+ trick
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 dxe5 Qh4+ g3 Qxe4+
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: If White grabs on e5 after ...e5, the queen check on h4 exploits the weakened king; after g3 the queen takes e4 with check and also eyes the h1 rook.

name: Fantasy 3.f3 e6: the solid anti-Fantasy
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The calm ...e6 keeps the d5 pawn firmly supported, turning the game toward a French-like structure where White's f3 looks misplaced.

name: Advance 3...c5: Nc6, pin with Bg4, then ...e6
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 Nf3 Nc6 c3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O cxd4 cxd4 Nge7
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Black strikes the base of the chain with a second c-pawn move, develops the queen knight, pins the f3 knight once it defends d4, and only then plays ...e6. The kingside knight goes to e7 on its way to f5 or g6, piling up on d4.

name: Advance 3...c5 4.dxc5: still ...Nc6 and win c5 back with the bishop
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the critical capture, Black keeps developing with ...Nc6 and ...Bg4; after ...e6 the dark bishop recaptures on c5 and the position is healthy.

name: Advance 3...Bf5 vs the Short system (Nf3/Be2)
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The classical answer to the Advance puts the bishop outside the chain first, then ...e6 and ...c5 to hit d4; Nf3, Be2 and castling is White's most testing calm setup.

name: Advance 3...Bf5 4.Nc3 e6 5.g4: give the bishop air
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When White throws the g-pawn forward early, the bishop must retreat to g6 and Black has to keep an eye on h-pawn pushes that could trap it.

name: Advance 3...Bf5 4.h4: answer with ...h5
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 h5
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: If White pushes the h-pawn early, Black must stop it with ...h5 at once; any natural move like ...e6 lets g4 and h5 trap the bishop.

name: Advance 4.h4 e6?? pitfall: the bishop gets trapped
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 e6 g4 Be4 f3 Bg6 h5
videoTitle: Learn the Caro-Kann Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A warning for Black: after the automatic ...e6, g4 and f3 chase the bishop and h5 leaves it with no squares at all.

name: Advance 3...c5 vs c3: Nc6, pin, ...e6, knight via e7 to f5
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Nge7
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: Levy's main recommendation: the same plan whether White captures or supports d4. Wait for Nf3, pin it, play ...e6, and route the king knight to f5 so both central pawns come under fire.

name: Panov with a fianchetto: ...g6 and ...Bg7
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: A favourite alternative to the solid ...e6: the bishop goes to g7 for quick development; even if White wins a central pawn, Black gets fast piece play against an isolated-looking centre.

name: Tartakower plan: Re8, knight d7-f8 guarding the king
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ exf6 c3 Bd6 Bd3 O-O Qc2 Re8+ Ne2 Nd7
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: After the e-pawn recapture, Black develops the bishop, castles, swings the rook to the e-file and reroutes the queen knight via d7 to f8, where it guards h7 and makes the king very hard to mate.

name: Fantasy 3...g6: ...Qb6 and grab b2
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Be3 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2 Rb1 Qa3
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: If White develops the bishop to e3 early, the queen jumps to b6 and takes b2; after Qd2 and Rb1 the queen slips back to a3 and Black keeps the extra pawn.

name: Fantasy 3...e5: the tricky dark-diagonal gambit
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e5 dxe5 Bc5
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: Not the theoretical best, but dangerous in practice: if White takes on e5, the bishop on c5 and the queen on b6 aim at g1 and f2, where f3 has weakened the king.

name: Two Knights: play it like a Tartakower
moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ exf6
videoTitle: How to CRUSH with the Caro-Kann!
idea: Against 2.Nc3 and 3.Nf3 Black can capture on e4 and recapture with the e-pawn after the knight trade, reaching the same simple bishop-out-and-castle setup.

name: Fantasy 3...dxe4 4.fxe4 e5 5.Nf3 Bg4 6.Bc4 Nd7 7.c3: the Qb3 fork
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 Bg4 Bc4 Nd7 c3 Ngf6 Qb3
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: After the forced ...e5 and ...Bg4, Bc4 threatens Bxf7+ followed by Nxe5, so Black must defend with ...Nd7; c3 then prepares Qb3, hitting f7 and b7 at once.

name: Fantasy 5...exd4: Bc4, castle, Ng5 and the f-file pin
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 exd4 Bc4 Nf6 O-O Bc5 Ng5 O-O Nxf7 Rxf7 Bxf7+ Kxf7 e5
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: If Black takes on d4, White ignores the pawn and develops fast. With the f-file open, Ng5 and the sacrifices on f7 end with e5 hitting the f6 knight, which is pinned to the king by the f1 rook.

name: Fantasy 4...Nf6?: kick the knight with e5 and c4
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4 Nb6 Nc3
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: If Black develops the knight instead of striking with ...e5, the e-pawn chases it, c4 chases it again, and White gets a massive centre with easy development.

name: Fantasy 3...g6: Nc3, Bg7, e5 and f4 (So/Caruana plan)
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e5
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: Against the fianchetto, White closes the centre with e5 and follows with f4, cutting the g7 bishop out of the game and keeping a space edge.

name: Advance 4.h4 h5 5.Bd3: trade the light bishops
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 h5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Nf3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: The classical way: having fixed h5 as a weakness and secured g5, White swaps Black's good bishop, then plays Nf3, a piece to g5, and expands with c4.

name: Advance 4.h4 h5 5.Bd3 ... 6...Qa5+ 7.Bd2 Qa6 8.e6!
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 h5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Qa5+ Bd2 Qa6 e6 Qxd3 cxd3 fxe6
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: When Black offers a queen trade on a6, White pushes e6 first; after the trade White has doubled d-pawns but Black's structure is wrecked, with holes on e5 and g5.

name: Advance 4.h4 h5 5.Bg5 Qb6 6.Bd3: the ...Qxb2 e6! gambit
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 h5 Bg5 Qb6 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Qxb2 e6 Qxa1 Qb3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Levy's favourite: if Black grabs b2, White gives up the rook with e6, keeps the pawn on e6 to hamper development, and plays Qb3 and Nf3 to trap the queen in the corner.

name: Advance 4.h4 h6 5.g4 Bh7 6.e6!
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4 h6 g4 Bh7 e6 fxe6 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: If Black allows the e6 thrust, take it: after ...fxe6 and the bishop trade, Black is left with a damaged structure, weak light squares and a buried dark bishop.

name: Advance 3...c5 4.dxc5 Nc6 5.Bb5
moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 Nc6 Bb5 e6 Be3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Taking on c5 and pinning with Bb5 stops Black's light bishop from developing comfortably; Be3 then supports the extra c-pawn.

name: Advance: ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Qb6, ...Nh6 (b2 is loose)
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Be2 Nh6 Bxh6 gxh6
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Black piles on d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6, then sends the king knight via h6 toward f5. If White trades on h6 the doubled pawns are acceptable: b2 hangs, White's pawns sit on dark squares, and Black gets the g-file.

name: Advance pitfall: 6.Bd3 cxd4 7.cxd4 Nxd4?? 8.Nxd4 Qxd4 9.Bb5+
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 Bb5+
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A warning: the d4 pawn only looks free. Grabbing it lets the bishop check from b5, uncovering an attack from the d1 queen on Black's queen. Finish development (for example ...Bd7) before taking.

name: Advance: ...cxd4 then ...Nh6-f5 hitting d4
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Be2 cxd4 cxd4 Nh6 Nc3 Nf5
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: After the pawn trade the knight reaches f5 through h6, and four Black pieces (queen, both knights, pawn on e6) are aimed at the d4 pawn.

name: Advance: ...Nge7 and if dxc5 then ...Qc7
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Be2 Nge7 dxc5 Qc7
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Routing the knight via e7 blocks the dark bishop, so if White takes on c5 Black does not recapture at once; ...Qc7 targets the e5 pawn instead.

name: Classical Steinitz: ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Be7
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 f4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Be3 Be7
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When White supports e5 with f4, Black hits d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6, develops the bishop to e7, and later expands with ...a6 and ...b5 on the queenside.

name: Winawer: pin the knight with ...Bb4
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The sharp alternative to ...Nf6 pins the c3 knight against the king and pressures e4; it leads to very theoretical positions.

name: Rubinstein with ...Nd7: ...Ngf6, ...b6, ...Bb7
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Nf3 Ngf6 Nxf6+ Nxf6 Bd3 b6 O-O Bb7
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Taking on e4 cuts down White's choices. The queen knight goes to d7 first so the king knight can recapture on f6; the light bishop is solved by ...b6 and ...Bb7, then ...Be7 and castling.

name: Fort Knox: ...Bd7-c6 to trade the problem bishop
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bd7 Nf3 Bc6 Bd3 Nd7 O-O Ngf6
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The usually passive French bishop goes to c6 where it can trade itself for White's strong e4 knight; Black then builds a rock-solid setup with ...Nf6, ...Nbd7 and a bishop on d6 or e7.

name: Tarrasch 3.Nd2 c5
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the knight on d2, Levy prefers striking d4 immediately; the knight on d2 cannot pressure d5 the way a c3 knight would.

name: Tarrasch 3.Nd2 h6 (planning ...g5-g4)
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 h6
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: An offbeat try: ...h6 prepares ...g5 and ...g4 to kick White's king knight off f3 before it settles.

name: Tarrasch 3.Nd2 Be7 (same ...g5 idea)
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Be7
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A flexible waiting move that keeps ...g5-g4 against a knight on f3 in reserve and avoids committing the c-pawn or the knight.

name: Early 2.Qe2: ...c5 and ...Nc6
moves: e4 e6 Qe2 c5
videoTitle: Learn the French Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: After 2.Qe2 the ...d5 push no longer works smoothly because the queen backs up e4, so Black just takes space with ...c5 and develops normally.

name: Rozman French: Rubinstein ...Nf6, ...gxf6, ...b6, ...Bb7
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ gxf6 Nf3 b6 Bd3 Bb7
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: Offer the knight trade at once and recapture toward the edge. With doubled f-pawns Black castles long; the bishop on b7 and a rook on g8 together aim at g2.

name: Rozman French vs Bb5: queen to d5 hits the bishop
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ gxf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Qd5
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: Against the pin on c6, the queen steps up to d5 and attacks the b5 bishop; Black is happy to end up with the only light-squared bishop, which works with a g-file rook against g2.

name: Rozman French vs 5.Ng3: ...c5
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Ng3 c5 dxc5 Qxd1+ Kxd1 Bxc5
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: If White avoids the trade, ...c5 is enough; taking on c5 forces a queen trade that leaves White's king stuck in the centre and Black ahead in development.

name: Rozman French vs 5.Ng3: ...h5
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Ng3 h5
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: A confusing practical choice: the h-pawn runs at the g3 knight, threatening ...h4 to drive it away.

name: Burn Variation 4.Bg5 dxe4: ...Be7 and if Bxf6 ...gxf6
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 dxe4 Nxe4 Be7 Bxf6 gxf6
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: Against the pin, Black blocks with ...Be7. If White gives up the bishop, recapturing with the g-pawn keeps the same doubled-f-pawn structure as the Rozman setup.

name: Burn Variation: 6.Nxf6+ Bxf6, castle, ...b6/...Bb7
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 dxe4 Nxe4 Be7 Nxf6+ Bxf6 Nf3 O-O
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: If the knight takes on f6 the bishop recaptures and the position is harmless: castle, play ...b6 and ...Bb7, and put a rook on d8 against the centre.

name: Exchange French with c4: ...Nf6, develop, castle short
moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Be7 Nf3 O-O
videoTitle: Crush Opponents with the Rozman French Defense
idea: If White plays an early c4 in the Exchange, Black stops thinking about castling long and simply develops and castles kingside.

name: Qa5 with ...Bg4: e6, Be7, castle short
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Be7
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: The queen hides on a5, the knight comes to f6, and the light bishop must get out (to g4) before ...e6 locks it in. Then ...Be7 and castling; ...c6 is always available to give the queen a retreat to c7.

name: Qa5 with ...Bg4 and ...Nc6: go long
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Nc6
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: If White does not occupy the centre aggressively, Black can develop the queen knight and castle queenside, which turns the game into an opposite-side race.

name: Qa5 Bg4: the critical h3, g4, Ne5 line
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bh5 g4 Bg6 Ne5
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: The computer-approved test of ...Bg4: White chases the bishop with pawns and lands a knight on e5. Rare below expert level, which is why Levy still recommends ...Bg4 over ...Bf5 for most players.

name: Qd6 setup: ...a6 first, then bishop, knight, long castle
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6 Nf3 a6
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: With the queen on d6, ...a6 is essential so a knight can never jump to b5 with tempo; Black then develops the bishop and queen knight and castles long to stack pressure on d4.

name: Qd8: retreat all the way home
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: The most modest retreat; the setup afterwards is the same as with ...Qa5 — develop, decide which side to castle by what White does.

name: 3.d4 Nf6 4.c4: ...Qe4+
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 c4 Qe4+
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: If White chases the queen with two pawns, the check on e4 is annoying: blocking with a bishop lets the queen pick off a pawn, and Black follows with central pressure and ...Bb4+.

name: 3.d4 e5: hit the centre and trade queens
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 e5 dxe5 Qxd1+ Kxd1
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: Against 3.d4 Black can strike with ...e5; if White takes, the queen trade costs White the right to castle.

name: 3.Nf3: ...Bg4, ...Nc6 and a quick long castle
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Nc6 O-O O-O-O
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: Against the more common 3.Nf3, Black develops the bishop with a pin, brings the knight out and castles long fast, often following up with ...e5.

name: 2.Nc3 dxe4 3.Nxe4 Qd5
moves: e4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Qd5
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: If White keeps the pawn tension with 2.Nc3, Black can take and hit the e4 knight with the queen; if it goes back to c3 the game is a normal Scandinavian.

name: Tennison Gambit 2.Nf3 dxe4 3.Ng5: ...e5
moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 e5
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: The simplest antidote to the Tennison: counterattack the g5 knight with ...e5 and finish development instead of clinging to every pawn.

name: Advance 2.e5: ...Bf5, ...e6, ...c5, ...Nc6
moves: e4 d5 e5 Bf5 d4 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nc6
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: If White pushes past d5, Black gets a Caro-Kann Advance structure a tempo up on the c-pawn: bishop out first, then ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6 against d4.

name: Leonhardt-style b4 gambit: just take
moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 b4 Qxb4
videoTitle: CRUSH People with the Scandinavian Defense!
idea: When White offers the b-pawn to deflect the queen, Black accepts, retreats the queen, and plays the normal setup a pawn up.

name: Accelerated Dragon: ...Nc6, ...g6, ...Bg7
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Delaying ...d6 and ...Nf6, Black fianchettoes at once. The same g6/Bg7 setup works against the closed Sicilian too, which keeps the repertoire small.

name: Closed Sicilian 2.Nc3: early ...a6 and ...b5
moves: e4 c5 Nc3 a6 g3 b5 Bg2 Bb7
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Instead of mirroring White's slow setup, Black grabs queenside space with ...a6 and ...b5, puts the bishop on b7 to rake the long diagonal, and later plays ...e6 and ...d5.

name: Pin Variation: ...e6, ...Nf6, ...Bb4
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A tricky ...e6 system for club players: after the knight trade on d4, Black pins the c3 knight and hits e4 immediately.

name: Four Knights: ...e6, ...Nf6, ...Nc6 (with ...Qb6 ideas)
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A tactical ...e6 system full of dark-square tricks; the queen often jumps to b6 to hit the d4 knight and b2.

name: Kalashnikov: early ...e5
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Kicking the centralised knight right away; Black accepts a hole on d5 in exchange for space and tempo.

name: Sveshnikov: ...Nf6 and ...e5
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The same ...e5 idea with the king knight already out; very theoretical and dynamic.

name: Classical: ...d6, ...Nf6, ...Nc6
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
videoTitle: The Sicilian Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The classical setup develops both knights to their natural squares and keeps all central options open.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6: e5, d4, Nf3, Bc4, Bb3 vs ...d5

name: Gotham Scandi vs Nf3/Bc4: ...Bb4, give the bishop for the knight, ...Qb6
